en: In the *Māratajjanīyasūtra* (WalA.1): "O Śramaṇas, having been exhorted by this instruction, they dwelt with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, as previously described, until Dūṣī Māra— looking for an opening,
seeking an opening— found no opening, found no foothold."

At that time, whatever faithful brahmin or householder was passing away, for the most part, upon the dissolution of the body after death, was reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a state of ruin, or in the hells.
Then, it occurred to Māra the Corrupter, who was watching for an opening and seeking an opening: "In this way, I do not find [an opportunity]."

"I find no opportunity or foothold among these shaven-headed ascetics; what if I were to influence the faithful brahmins and householders in such a way that, upon seeing the ascetics who are virtuous and endowed with good qualities, they would honor them, revere them, respect them, and worship them?
In this way, there might arise for the ascetics honor, reverence, and worship in the minds of others."

"I find a point of vulnerability, I find a foothold, I find a basis for alteration— just as I, seeking an entry-point and searching for a flaw, obtain an entry-point and obtain a basis. At that time, faithful brahmins and householders were so thoroughly influenced that, upon seeing virtuous and qualified ascetics,
they honored them, revered them, esteemed them, and worshiped them.
Furthermore, alms-food designated by Brahmins and householders has now been set aside for those who have undertaken the training. They say:
"May the ascetics who are virtuous and endowed with qualities accept from us this alms-food designated for the training; that will lead to our welfare, benefit, and happiness for a long time."
Furthermore, they would display new, unwashed robes with long fringes at the entrances of the streets and say:
"Let the virtuous and meritorious ascetics tread upon these new, unwashed robes with their feet; that will lead to our long-term welfare, benefit, and happiness."
WalA.7 Furthermore, they even display the hair—the head-hair—of the śramaṇas at the entrances of the streets and say:
"Let those endowed with virtue tread upon these hairs of the head with their feet; that will lead to our long-term welfare, benefit, and happiness.
WalA.8 Furthermore, having seen śramaṇas who are virtuous and endowed with qualities, they embrace them with all their limbs and enter into their homes.

They had them sit on prepared seats and spoke thus: "May our śramaṇas, who are virtuous and endowed with qualities, sit upon these prepared seats; that will be for our long-term welfare, benefit, and happiness.
Then the disciples of the Perfectly Awakened One Krakasunda—being honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped—approached where the Perfectly Awakened One Krakasunda was.

O Śramaṇas, having been instructed by the Perfectly Awakened One Krakasunda with this very instruction, they dwell contemplating the impermanence of conditioned phenomena, as described previously, up to contemplating their relinquishment. Therein, Māra the Corrupter, looking for an opening and seeking an opportunity, finds no opening and finds no foothold.

At that time, whatever faithful brahmin or householder was dying, for the most part, upon the dissolution of the body after death, was reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world, among the gods.
Then, Dūṣī Māra, looking for an opportunity, thought: "Even so, I do not find [an opening] among these shavelings..."
"Since I cannot find an opportunity or a foothold against these ascetics who observe things in this way, what if I were to approach the Venerable Vidūra with my own body?
On one occasion, the Tathāgata Krakasunda, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, was staying in a *sālā* in the brahmin village of Vidūrapura, with the Venerable Vidūra as his attendant monk.

Then, when that very night had passed, in the forenoon, the Perfectly Awakened One Krakasunda dressed himself, took his bowl and robe, and entered the brahmin village for alms, accompanied by the Venerable [Vidūra].
With the venerable Vidūra as his attendant bhikṣu.
Then Māra Dūṣī, having assumed the form of a youth and taken up a pebble, struck the head of the venerable Vidūra, so that blood flowed from his mouth.
Nevertheless, with his head broken and blood dripping from his mouth, the venerable Vidūra followed closely behind the Perfectly Awakened One, Krakasunda.

The Perfectly Awakened One, Krakasunda, saw the Evil One, Pāpiman, looking back with his entire body like an elephant with a glance toward the right, as the head of the venerable Vidūra was broken and blood was trickling from his mouth. Having seen this, he struck him and proclaimed: "This is the powerful Māra Dūṣī; this very Māra Dūṣī did not know moderation."
WalB.9. "In this matter, O Evil One, because of his lack of compliance, the Tathāgata has indeed acted and has made his intention known.
WalB.10. Then that Māra Dūṣī was cast down from that place all around into the great Avīci hell.

WalB.11. At that time, there were four names for the great Avīci hell: "Avīci," "The Uninterrupted," "The Hundred-Pointed Spike," and also "To be Experienced Individually" and "The Six Bases of Contact."
Thus it is also said.
